chapters.title: The Many Stories of Diwali
chapters.location: Across India and the Indian diaspora
chapters.summary: Diwali is a major festival celebrated through many regional, religious and cultural traditions. Its stories, rituals and meanings vary across communities.
chapters.historical_note: Diwali does not have a single origin story shared by all communities. Different traditions connect the festival with different religious and cultural narratives.

cinematic.opening: A night of lamps begins across ancient cities, villages and riverbanks.

scenes.title: Night of Lamps
scenes.description: Oil lamps begin glowing as evening falls.

scenes.title: Ancient Celebrations
scenes.description: Traditional communities gather for seasonal celebrations.

scenes.title: Many Traditions
scenes.description: Different communities develop their own stories and rituals.

chapters.title: Roots and Traditions
chapters.summary: The festival developed through diverse traditions involving lamps, worship, family gatherings, food, gifts, markets and community celebrations.
chapters.historical_note: Practices associated with Diwali differ significantly between regions and communities.

cinematic.opening: Across India, homes and streets slowly transform as lamps are prepared for the festival.

scenes.title: Preparing the Diyas
scenes.description: Clay lamps are prepared and filled with oil.

scenes.title: Decorating Homes
scenes.description: Homes are decorated with lamps, flowers and rangoli.

scenes.title: Festival Markets
scenes.description: Markets become active with sweets, clothing, decorations and gifts.

chapters.title: Rama, Sita and the Journey Home
chapters.summary: One widely observed Hindu tradition connects Diwali with Rama's return to Ayodhya after fourteen years of exile.
chapters.historical_note: This chapter represents the Ramayana tradition and should be presented as a religious and cultural narrative rather than independently verified historical documentation.

cinematic.opening: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana begin their journey home as the sun begins to set.

scenes.title: The Journey Home
scenes.description: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana begin their journey toward Ayodhya.

scenes.title: Across the Landscape
scenes.description: The journey continues through forests and landscapes as evening approaches.

scenes.title: Ayodhya Awaits
scenes.description: The people of Ayodhya prepare lamps for Rama's return.

scenes.title: The City of Lamps
scenes.description: Ayodhya is illuminated with rows of lamps as the returning figures approach.

scenes.title: A Celebration of Light
scenes.description: The return becomes a symbolic celebration of light, hope and renewal.

chapters.title: Krishna and Narakasura
chapters.summary: In another Hindu tradition, Naraka Chaturdashi is associated with Krishna's victory over Narakasura.
chapters.historical_note: The story belongs to Hindu religious tradition and has different regional forms and interpretations.

cinematic.opening: Before sunrise, lamps illuminate a city preparing for Naraka Chaturdashi.

scenes.title: Before Sunrise
scenes.description: The city prepares for the festival before dawn.

scenes.title: The Battle
scenes.description: A traditional depiction of Krishna confronting Narakasura.

scenes.title: Victory
scenes.description: The story concludes with the defeat of Narakasura.

chapters.title: Lakshmi and the Festival of Prosperity
chapters.summary: Lakshmi Puja is an important part of Diwali observance for many Hindu communities, with prayers associated with prosperity, abundance and well-being.
chapters.historical_note: The form and timing of Lakshmi worship varies between regions and communities.

cinematic.opening: As darkness falls, homes are illuminated and families prepare for Lakshmi Puja.

scenes.title: Preparing the Home
scenes.description: Families clean and decorate their homes before the evening worship.

scenes.title: Lakshmi Puja
scenes.description: Families gather for prayers and traditional rituals.

scenes.title: Light and Prosperity
scenes.description: Rows of lamps create a warm atmosphere around homes and temples.

chapters.title: Mahavira and Jain Diwali
chapters.summary: For Jains, Diwali is associated with the liberation, or nirvana, of Mahavira, the twenty-fourth Tirthankara.
chapters.historical_note: Jain communities observe Diwali through religious practices connected with Mahavira's nirvana.

cinematic.opening: Quiet lamps glow around Jain temples as devotees gather in remembrance.

scenes.title: The Temple
scenes.description: A Jain temple is illuminated during the festival.

scenes.title: Remembering Mahavira
scenes.description: Devotees gather for prayer and remembrance.

scenes.title: The Light of Knowledge
scenes.description: Lamps symbolize spiritual illumination and remembrance.

chapters.title: Bandi Chhor Divas
chapters.summary: Sikh communities observe Bandi Chhor Divas around the same period as Diwali, commemorating the release of Guru Hargobind and other prisoners.
chapters.historical_note: Bandi Chhor Divas is a distinct Sikh observance with its own historical and religious significance.

cinematic.opening: The Golden Temple complex begins to glow with lamps as evening arrives.

scenes.title: The Golden Temple
scenes.description: The Harmandir Sahib is illuminated during the celebration.

scenes.title: Bandi Chhor
scenes.description: The tradition remembers Guru Hargobind and the release of prisoners.

scenes.title: Community Celebration
scenes.description: Families and communities gather for prayers and celebration.

chapters.title: Diwali Today
chapters.location: India and the global Indian diaspora
chapters.summary: Today Diwali is celebrated through family gatherings, prayers, travel, food, shopping, gifts, decorations, community events and public celebrations.
chapters.historical_note: Modern Diwali celebrations combine religious observances with regional customs and contemporary social and commercial practices.

cinematic.opening: Modern cities begin to glow as families prepare for another night of Diwali.

scenes.title: Modern Cities
scenes.description: Cities across India light up during the festival.

scenes.title: Families Together
scenes.description: Families gather, exchange gifts and share festive meals.

scenes.title: Diwali Around the World
scenes.description: Indian communities celebrate Diwali in cities across the world.

chapters.title: The Changing Festival
chapters.summary: Modern Diwali celebrations also bring discussions about air quality, noise, waste, public safety and more sustainable ways to celebrate.
chapters.historical_note: Environmental and public-health impacts associated with fireworks have been documented by Indian environmental authorities. The scale and effects vary by location, weather and celebration patterns.

cinematic.opening: After the celebration, a city slowly becomes quiet as the final lamps continue to glow.

scenes.title: The Celebration
scenes.description: Fireworks and lights fill the night sky.

scenes.title: The Morning After
scenes.description: Streets and neighborhoods begin returning to normal after the celebrations.

scenes.title: A Changing Conversation
scenes.description: Communities discuss cleaner, safer and more responsible ways to celebrate.

chapters.title: The Future of Diwali
chapters.location: India and communities around the world
chapters.summary: Diwali continues to evolve as communities balance traditional rituals with changing technology, lifestyles and environmental awareness.
chapters.historical_note: The future of the festival will depend on how communities continue to preserve traditions while adapting celebrations to contemporary circumstances.

cinematic.opening: One by one, the lamps of the present become lights leading toward the future.

scenes.title: Tradition Continues
scenes.description: Traditional lamps and rituals remain part of the celebration.

scenes.title: New Generations
scenes.description: Younger generations carry familiar traditions into new environments.

scenes.title: A Festival That Evolves
scenes.description: The festival continues to change while retaining its cultural significance.
